newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL share market rebounds to end firmer.
newsitem.headline: KL share market rebounds to end firmer.

text.p: Afternoon buying helped the Kuala Lumpur share market end on positive ground for the first time this week.

But sentiment remained brittle on the uncertainty surrounding the late Proton chief Yahaya Ahmad's companies, weakness on Wall Street and the prospect of a shorter settlement period for stock trades, dealers said.

After posting losses through midday, the Composite Index of 100 large stocks regained its composure to close up 5.05 points or 0.40 percent to 1,252.28, its high for the day. The Second Board index gained 4.48 points to 646.44.
Turnover topped 449 million shares, versus 400 million on Tuesday. Gainers led losers by 420 to 174.

The Composite Index's recovery "is encouraging", said Patrick Zecha, head of research at South Johor Securities. "The CI was trying to hold at psychological support of 1,250. But the market still needs to stabilise."

Dealers said they had received calls from clients seeking advice about their holdings in Yahaya-linked stocks. Nine of his companies were suspended on Tuesday following news of his death in a helicopter accident. Foreign clients are mainly concerned about who will succeed Yahaya, a dealer said.
